findings.source_passage: It touches one's sense of honor, particularly if you come of an old established family in the land, the Van Rensselaers, or Randolphs, or Hardicanutes. And more than all, if just previous to putting your hand into the tar-pot, you have been lording it as a country schoolmaster
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'No, when I go to sea'
findings.why_it_matters: The Van Rensselaers/Randolphs/Hardicanutes joke and the schoolmaster-to-tar-pot setup are what make the following 'transition is a keen one... from a schoolmaster to a sailor' line land. Draft keeps the punchline but cuts the setup, leaving 'schoolmaster' unmotivated and the mock-aristocratic voice erased.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least the Van Rensselaers/Randolphs/Hardicanutes clause and the tar-pot/schoolmaster setup so the Seneca-and-Stoics sentence has its comic scaffolding.

findings.source_passage: weighed, I mean, in the scales of the New Testament?
findings.source_locator: 'What of it, if some old hunks...' paragraph, preceding 'Who ain't a slave?'
findings.why_it_matters: The 'scales of the New Testament' phrase is the theological pivot that sets up 'Who ain't a slave?' — it supplies the mock-scriptural register that makes the democratic-leveling aphorism bite. Its removal flattens the passage's signature irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinstate 'What does that indignity amount to, weighed, I mean, in the scales of the New Testament?' before the Gabriel sentence.

findings.source_passage: Its extreme downtown is the battery, where that noble mole is washed by waves... Look at the crowds of water-gazers there. Go from Corlears Hook to Coenties Slip, and from thence, by Whitehall, northward.
findings.why_it_matters: The specific NYC topography (Battery, Corlears Hook, Coenties Slip, Whitehall) grounds the 'insular Manhattoes' motif in concrete circumambulation; cutting all place-names thins the sustained set piece the pre-pass flagged as voice-establishing.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least one of the place-name clauses (e.g., 'Go from Corlears Hook to Coenties Slip, and from thence, by Whitehall, northward') to preserve the circumambulation cadence.

findings.source_passage: Tell me, does the magnetic virtue of the needles of the compasses of all those ships attract them thither?
findings.source_locator: end of the 'But look! here come more crowds' paragraph
findings.why_it_matters: The signature cascading genitive ('needles of the compasses of all those ships') is a characteristic Melvillean rhythmic flourish that closes the water-gazers section; its loss removes the rhetorical button on the paragraph.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'magnetic virtue of the needles of the compasses' sentence as the paragraph's close.

summary: Core signatures (opening, November cadence, Cato, Manhattoes, water-gazers, Narcissus, Who ain't a slave?, playbill, hooded phantom) are intact; two medium losses in middle voice passages (New Testament scales; Van Rensselaers/tar-pot setup) weaken but do not break the chapter.
